name: Pindi Chole
steps: Soak chickpeas in plenty of water for 8–12 hours in the refrigerator, then discard the soaking water and rinse. Tie the tea leaves securely in a clean food-safe muslin bag.
Boil chickpeas with the measured fresh water and tea bag, then simmer partly covered for 75–95 minutes until easily crushed. Add hot water if needed to keep them covered. Remove the tea bag.
Drain the chickpeas, saving 250 ml cooking liquid. Toss them with coriander powder, cumin powder, pomegranate powder, amchur, chilli powder, garam masala and salt.
Heat ghee in a wide pan, sizzle cumin seeds, then add sliced ginger and chilli for 1 minute. Add the spiced chickpeas and reserved liquid and cook for 10–12 minutes, turning gently.
Stop when the spices cling to the chickpeas and little free liquid remains. Check that the centres are completely tender and serve with separately prepared bread.
passiveTime: Soak chickpeas for 8–12 hours in the refrigerator.
notes: Base recipe for 4 adults. Cooking times are estimates; follow the texture and doneness cues. Jain suitability follows your saved ingredient choices.
